chapter: Technique, jam sessions, audiences and records
title: White musicians who sat in
summary: Smith recalls Henry Busse and an unnamed tenor, and a trumpeter called Neal who followed Charlie Parker.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Can you remember the names of any other White musicians who used to come and sit in? Or who were good enough to come and sit in.
Oh yeah-yeah. A gang of them come down there. Let me see. Henry Busse(?), a trumpet player.
Yeah. And he had a tenor player. I can't think of this tenor player's name, but he used to come in to Kansas City all the time and sit in with us.

Yeah! Great tenor player. I can't even call his name. But over at the Lone Star, where Pete Johnson and Joe Turner would work, he'd come over there and sit in. Every time he'd come to town -- a tenor player.

And let me see who else. A White trumpet player would come there sometimes, too. I can't think of his name. But a boy named Neal in Kansas City hung around with Charlie Parker all the time. He just followed him (?).
Yeah, a White fellow. He played trumpet. They called him Neal. I think he probably got with Charlie Barnet a while.
Yeah, he left there, and I don't know... We didn't hear what happened after he left Charlie Barnet.
